1. The Transparency Dilemma in Mathematical Graphics

In mathematical animations (such as Riemann sum visualizations, complex Riemannian surfaces, intersecting manifolds, Venn diagrams, and overlapping geometric contours), multiple transparent surfaces frequently intersect in 3D/2D space.
Standard WebGPU rasterization evaluates transparency via **alpha blending with depth writes disabled**. However:

items: **CPU Depth Sorting Fails on Intersecting Meshes**: When two transparent triangles intersect each other, neither triangle is strictly "in front" of the other. Any triangle-level sorting order causes rendering artifacts along the intersection line.
**Dynamic Topology Morphing**: In Retiam, shapes morph continuously. Sorting tens of thousands of triangles on the CPU every frame destroys 60 FPS performance.
**Multi-Layer Stencil & Vector Overlays**: Overlapping vector paths with translucent fills require exact order-independent color accumulation.

blocks.text: To solve this, Retiam implements **Per-Pixel Linked List Order-Independent Transparency (PPLL OIT)** directly in WebGPU storage buffers.
2. Architecture Overview
Retiam provides two distinct OIT architectures coordinated under [`PPLLManager.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/ppll_oit/PPLLManager.ts):

blocks.text: 3. Global A-Buffer vs. Local K-Buffer Implementation
A. Global Dynamic A-Buffer ([PPLLManagerGlobal.ts](../src/engine/render/pplloit/PPLLManagerGlobal.ts))
Uses a shared global fragment node pool with dynamic atomic allocation:

items: **Head Pointer Buffer**: `width * height * 4` bytes (`Uint32Array`), initialized to `0xFFFFFFFF` (`NULL`) at the beginning of each frame.
**Atomic Counter Buffer**: A 4-byte `atomic<u32>` buffer tracking the total number of fragments written across the entire screen.
**Node Pool Buffer**: Sized to `width * height * maxLayers * 12` bytes:

B. Local Fixed K-Buffer ([PPLLManagerLocal.ts](../src/engine/render/pplloit/PPLLManagerLocal.ts))
For platforms with atomic contention limits or bounded layer requirements:

items: Replaces the global linked list with a per-pixel array of `maxLayers` (typically 8 layers).
**Pixel Counter Buffer**: `width * height * 4` bytes, holding a per-pixel atomic counter.
**Node Pool Buffer**: `width * height * maxLayers * 8` bytes (`color: u32, depth: f32`).
Prevents unbounded global atomic serialization at the cost of fixed memory layout per pixel.
